perspective:
**Harold Padilla’s available information:**

- Harold is a project manager. He feels frustrated, anxious, and at his wit’s end because his project is not progressing and he believes his team is not performing well due to lack of motivation.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a friend and police officer whom he relies on for advice and support. Harold arranges to meet Arthur at a local coffee shop.
- At that meeting, Harold tells Arthur his team seems completely unmotivated and it is affecting progress. He hears Arthur say that motivation can be tricky and ask whether Harold has tried understanding what drives each team member individually.
- Harold admits he has focused mainly on project goals and deadlines, not personal motivations. He hears Arthur advise that people need to feel valued and understood personally, and suggest one-on-one conversations. Harold agrees to try it, thanks Arthur, and feels hopeful.
- Harold later tells his team he wants quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them and believes this will help them work better together. He hears Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they are open to it. Harold says he will schedule time with each of them and asks them to make the project a success together.
- Harold notices that the team still is not responding well to the new strategies. He feels disappointed and worried about the project’s future. He returns to Arthur and tells him the suggestions did not work.
- Harold hears Arthur suggest there may be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper. Harold decides to set up another round of meetings.
- Harold then holds one-on-one meetings. He tells team members he has noticed performance issues and asks them to share concerns or problems.
- Harold hears Team Member 1 say there is tension between a few people that is affecting work. Harold says he will look into resolving these conflicts.
- Harold hears Team Member 2 say they feel overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, which makes it hard to stay motivated. Harold says he understands, will see if tasks can be redistributed, and tells them their well-being is important.
- Afterward, Harold feels optimistic and empowered. He believes addressing individual concerns will improve team performance.
- Harold tells the team he has heard their concerns and will implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment.
- Harold hears Team Member 1 say that sounds great and will help them work better together. He hears Team Member 2 agree and say it is good that their concerns are being addressed.
- Harold tells the team he is glad, asks them to work together to make the project a success, and says their input and well-being are crucial.
